item.title: Walter Probe Weighs on Carvana as Investors Suspect Share Sale
item.description: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. are extending losses Tuesday, hurt by concerns that one of the company’s largest investors — billionaire Mark Walter — may sell down his stake as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.
item.dc:creator: Georgie McKay

item.title: University of California System Offloads $1 Billion of Private Equity Stakes
item.description: The University of California system sold $1 billion of private equity stakes to HarbourVest Partners, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Singh

item.title: Bloomberg Surveillance 8/18/2026
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Where Investors Can Hide From Shocks | Open Interest 8/18/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Bond anxiety is building around the globe. Ed Yardeni weighs the risks from AI and the Fed. Home Depot puts the consumer to the test. Plus, JPMorgan’s Gabriela Santos on shelter from market shocks, Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy on the economics of enterprise AI, and Goldman Sachs strikes another deal to expand its $4 trillion asset-management business. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BP Joins Venezuelan Oil Trade to Challenge Trafigura and Vitol
item.description: BP Plc has become the latest foreign company to begin trading Venezuelan oil since the US removed former President Nicolás Maduro, following in the footsteps of Trafigura Group and Vitol Group.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Kassai

item.title: Starwood Team Lends $672 Million for US Outdoor Storage Lots
item.description: Starwood Property Trust Inc. and Realterm, a global investment manager focused on transportation, provided a $672 million loan for a group of US industrial outdoor storage lots.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Wong

item.title: Stocks Take Hit as Bond Selloff Saps Risk Appetite
item.description: A selloff in chipmakers sent stocks lower, with the market also falling as inflation angst and rising government debt kept bond yields elevated. Longer-dated bonds are at the epicenter of anxiety about everything from inflation to the debt-laden artificial-intelligence boom. Liz Ann Sonders, Chief Investment Strategist at Charles Schwab, discusses the gap between sell-side consensus and buy-side expectations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin Whales End Selling Spree, Adding $2.9 Billion in 60 Days
item.description: Bitcoin has spent months mired in a slump that has driven out retail traders, drained billions from crypto funds and turned one of its biggest buyers into a seller. Now, investors searching for signs of a bottom are getting a modicum of relief from an old source: Bitcoin whales are buying again.
item.dc:creator: Vildana Hajric and Olga Kharif

item.title: Raw Sugar Advances to 14-Month High on Global Supply Concerns
item.description: Raw sugar futures rose to the highest in more than a year as India, the world’s second-largest producer, is considering cutting import duties on the commodity in the latest sign of global supply constraint.
item.dc:creator: Ana Mano

item.title: Chip Stocks Get Hit as Global Bond Anxiety Builds
item.description: A selloff in chipmakers sent stocks lower, with the market also falling as inflation angst and rising government debt kept bond yields elevated. John Mowrey, CIO at NFJ Investment Group, discusses AI capex spending and equities reaching all-time highs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bank of Israel's Yaron Says Next Policy Meeting Will Be a Live One
item.description: Bank of Israel Governor Amir Yaron says Israel's economy has shown resilience during the war in Iran but warns there's a big fiscal policy challenge ahead. He speaks with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bath & Body Works Surges on Stock Recommendation; Klarna Drops on Guidance | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Shares of Klarna (KLAR) plunged in premarket trading after the payments company reported full year revenue and gross merchandise value guidance that missed expectations. The company cited foreign exchange pressures and volumes in Germany, even as it reported a profit beat for the second straight quarter. - Shares of Amylyx Pharmaceuticals (AMLX) extended its rally in the early session to as much as 54%, after the drug developer said a late-stage trial of its experimental drug met its primary endpoint as a treatment for patients who experience low blood sugar levels following bariatric surgery. - Shares of Bath & Body Works (BBWI) surged ahead of the opening bell after Citi raised its recommendation on the stock to buy from neutral. Analyst Paul Lejuez cited a favorable risk/reward outlook in his note. The company is slated to release earnings next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The RealReal Bets on Luxury Resale Boom
item.description: The RealReal CEO Rati Levesque joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why resale prices are increasingly shaping what shoppers buy new, with more than 80% of Gen Z and millennial customers checking secondhand values first. She also reveals which unexpected fashion pieces are appreciating, and why AI still can’t fully replace human luxury authenticators. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BofA Sees Nvidia Trading at Up to 50% Discount on AI Risks
item.description: Nvidia Corp. shares could be trading at a discount of as much as 50%, as investors overstate risks related to the leader in artificial intelligence chips, according to Bank of America.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: EM Rally Hits a Wall as Global Yields Climb, Oil Prices Rally
item.description: Emerging markets lost momentum on Tuesday as a surge in long-term US Treasury yields collided with renewed tensions in the Middle East, ending a four-day winning streak for stocks and driving borrowing costs higher across developing economies.
item.dc:creator: David Feliba and Peter Laca

item.title: US Stocks Drop, Led by Tech, as Bond-Yield Spike Sparks Angst
item.description: US stocks fell on Tuesday, led by a slump in technology shares, as elevated bond yields and gains in oil prices prompted investors to pare back some of their riskier trades including bets on AI.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: Long-Term Debt Costs Soar to Highest in Decades as Bonds Slump
item.description: Longer-maturity bonds are at the epicenter of investor angst about everything from inflation to the debt-laden artificial-intelligence boom — and governments are paying the price.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Matthew Burgess

item.title: Gold Falls as Traders Weigh US Inflation, Rates Amid Bond Rout
item.description: Gold declined as traders weighed the outlook for US inflation and interest rates amid a global government bond rout.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie, Jack Ryan and Yvonne Yue Li

item.title: Chip Rout Pulls Stocks Down as Bond Angst Lingers: Markets Wrap
item.description: A selloff in chipmakers sent stocks lower, with the market also falling as inflation anxiety and rising government debt kept bond yields elevated.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Guggenheim 77% Earnings Hit Stems From Unit Whistleblower Tagged
item.description: A steep decline in Guggenheim Investments’ second-quarter earnings was driven by a delay in reporting certain fee revenue from its private investments unit, where accounting was the subject of a whistleblower report that helped spark a wider probe into Mark Walter’s empire.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Basu, Sridhar Natarajan and Zachary R. Mider
